fields.label: Drift Class
fields.description: A slug from chat.governance.drift_rules.CLASSES. Deliberately NOT a D-number: the tokens D1-D7 are already cited in shipped code with a different meaning (the prompt-vs-code divergences in docs/chat-phase6-plan.md), and two meanings for one token inside one package is a permanent tax on every reader.

fields.label: State
fields.description: Accepted means 'we know, and we are not fixing it'. Re-observing does not undo it — otherwise the operator who triaged this gets it back tomorrow. Cleared is terminal; a recurrence opens a new row rather than reopening this one.

fields.label: Scope
fields.description: The object this finding is about. Two objects with the same problem are two findings; one object observed nightly is one.

fields.label: Report Key
fields.description: drift_class::scope. Indexed and deliberately NOT unique: a cleared finding that recurs must be able to open a second row with the same key, and a unique index would make the recurrence fail to insert instead.

fields.label: Observations
fields.description: How many scans have seen this finding. A finding seen once may be a race; one seen thirty nights running is a decision nobody has made.

fields.label: Evidence
fields.description: The positive fact that proves the mirror acted on this object. Copied from drift_rules.EVIDENCE at write time so the row still explains itself after the constant is edited. A drift class with no evidence entry cannot be emitted at all — every class here fires on something that HAPPENED, never on an empty column, because an empty column is a fact about the configuration rather than about the mirror.

fields.label: Detail
fields.description: Identifiers, states, counts and timestamps. NEVER message text: this table is a census of what diverged, not a copy of what was said, and a drift report holding bodies would be a second transcript outside the membership model.

fields.label: Clear Note
fields.description: Written by the scan when the condition stops being observed, not by a human: a finding the system can see is gone says so itself, so the board shows what is diverged now rather than everything that ever was.
